name: Eleazar
overview: Eleazar was a male descendant of Parosh noted in the book of Ezra. His distinct identification comes from being among those who had married foreign wives, a matter of concern addressed in the post-exilic community. No specific tribal affiliation or additional personal details are recorded for him.
namesAndTitles: The name Eleazar means 'G-d is a help,' reflecting a common theophoric element in Hebrew names that acknowledges divine assistance. This proper name is recorded in Ezra 10:25 without indication that it was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Eleazar as a descendant of Parosh, establishing a familial link important for understanding his place within the returning exiles. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Eleazar's significance lies in his representation of the challenges faced by the returning Israelites in maintaining covenant purity after the exile. His mention as one who married a foreign wife highlights the community's efforts to restore holiness according to God's commands. This underscores the broader narrative of repentance and renewal central to the post-exilic period.
